US and Denmark Finalize Greenland Security Agreement

The United States and Denmark have reached an agreement that grants the U.S. permanent control over security matters in Greenland. President Donald Trump announced the deal, stating it allows the U.S. "permanent control over security, and all other needs" in the territory. The agreement was made with Denmark, with Greenland remaining under Danish sovereignty. Trump indicated the deal would facilitate an expanded U.S. military presence. While the U.S. gains significant security access, the island's administration remains with Denmark.
